output.key_objective: Design a multi-agent system for student course registration
plan_steps: Define agent roles, responsibilities, and course registration requirements
Design agent coordination workflows, data models, and conflict resolution logic
Prototype system and evaluate registration accuracy, scalability, and student experience

output.analysis: Multi-agent system for student course registration is technically feasible using existing patterns: Advisor Agent (eligibility, prerequisites), Scheduler Agent (timetable, seat allocation), Conflict Resolver Agent (overlaps, waitlists, priority rules), and Orchestrator with shared data model linked to SIS/LMS. Core logic (constraints, capacity, prerequisites) is deterministic and well-suited to rule-based validation with LLM agents handling natural language intent and exceptions. Main feasibility constraints are real-time concurrency at registration peaks, strict consistency with authoritative SIS as source of truth, and integration with legacy systems. Prototype can validate accuracy and UX quickly, but production requires transactional guarantees, auditability, and FERPA compliance that pure agent-to-agent negotiation cannot provide alone.
identified_risks: Race conditions and overbooking during peak concurrent registration without transactional seat holds
Data inconsistency between agents and authoritative SIS due to stale caches or delayed sync
Deadlock or livelock in agent negotiation and priority/waitlist conflict resolution
Unfair allocation or bias in conflict resolution logic violating academic policies
FERPA and privacy breach from agents over-sharing student records across contexts
Scalability failure and latency spikes during enrollment windows degrading student experience
Hallucinated prerequisites, course availability, or requirements causing incorrect enrollments
